title: Simplified medical reports improve comprehension in a randomized reader study
summary: A Mainz study randomly assigned 576 adult participants to an original or GPT-4-simplified version of one of five German medical documents. Among 439 completed comprehension questionnaires, simplified texts generally produced more correct answers, with the pathology comparison not statistically significant. This measures immediate understanding of selected, researcher-checked texts, not improved treatment adherence or health outcomes. Single-site recruitment, incomplete questionnaires and only one text pair per document type limit generalization.

source_review.scope: Primary model operation, randomized reader-study Methods, results and limitations; exact front-matter identity/date and current PubMed/PMC correction/retraction metadata. Supplementary questionnaire and independent semantic validation were not inspected.

evidence.tested: Randomized assignment to original or pre-generated simplified German medical reports, followed by immediate multiple-choice comprehension questions; 576 participants, with 439 completed comprehension questionnaires.
evidence.unknown: Generalization beyond five selected text pairs and a single German clinical department, long-term retention, adherence and clinical outcomes remain unestablished. Education/health-literacy measures were not collected; results include incomplete questionnaires. Output generation settings are described inconsistently as configured parameters and default web sessions; the represented result concerns the actual selected texts.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4 rewrites physician-authored medical reports into lay language; those generated texts form the experimental intervention used to test readers’ immediate comprehension.
